newsitem.title: SPAIN: Venezuela's Casas says inflation key to exports.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Casas says inflation key to exports.

text.p: Venezuela will be able to consider stimulating exports via exchange rates once its inflation rate has stabilised, Central Bank Governor Antonio Casas said on Thursday.

"We need to stabilise inflation in order to grow. When we start to grow, which I hope will be this year, we'll start to think about the exchange rate as a stimulus for exports," he said at a news conference in Madrid.
The official target for Venezuelan inflation this year is 25 percent, with economic growth seen at 4.0 percent.
Promoting exports is important, but it cannot be achieved through exchange rates alone, Casas said.
"One doesn't fuel (exports) simply with exchange rates...For that to happen, I need something to export."
He said lower inflation was necessary to control exporters' costs "rather than liberalising the dollar/bolivar, allowing the bolivar to depreciate and depreciate."
Curbing inflation also requires strict fiscal and monetary policy, Casas added.

"The forex system we have at the moment aims to anchor inflation, but inflation can't be anchored just with exchange rates. For this to be effective, there has (to) be a very restrictive fiscal policy and a very restrictive monetary policy," he said.
"But undoubtedly, within the stabilisation model we have, the exchange rate plays a role, too."
Venezuela's January inflation rose 2.6 percent month-over-month.
